question.text: An option writer who sells a call option at a premium of Rs. 150 with strike price Rs. 18,000 will make a profit when:

answer.text: The underlying price stays below Rs. 18,150 at expiry
The underlying price rises above Rs. 18,000 at expiry
The underlying price falls to zero at expiry
The underlying price equals exactly Rs. 18,000 at expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: For a short call, the break-even point (BEP) is Strike + Premium = 18,000 + 150 = Rs. 18,150. The writer makes a profit when the underlying price at expiry is less than 18,150, breaks even at 18,150, and starts making a loss when the underlying price exceeds 18,150. Maximum profit (the full premium of Rs. 150) is realised when the underlying expires at or below the strike of Rs. 18,000 and the call expires worthless. The Trap: The writer can still profit when the underlying is slightly above the strike, as long as the underlying is below the BEP (Strike + Premium). The profit zone is not defined by the strike alone. Note: Short call profit condition (per workbook page 69): Underlying at expiry < Strike + Premium, with maximum profit equal to the premium received when the option expires worthless.
